article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Sour Apple × Animal Cookies
Breeder: Sensi Seeds
THC Content: 21%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet apple, spicy pine, earth, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 63–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 450 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 550 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Pumpkin Spice earns its name in an unusual way. There is no promise that every flower will smell exactly like a cup of autumn coffee or a slice of pumpkin pie; instead, the cultivar builds the association through warm spice, sweet fruit, earth, herbs, and an unexpected apple note that develops after curing. Sensi Seeds created it from Sour Apple and Animal Cookies, bringing bright fruit and cerebral energy together with Cookies-family density, resin, and heavier physical effects. The finished plant sits almost perfectly in the middle at 50% indica and 50% sativa, yet its growth pattern leans noticeably toward the indica side with short stature, tight internodes, and substantial foliage.

The flowering phase tells a different story. Long, spear-shaped buds rise above the compact frame, showing more of the sativa influence while retaining the firmness and weight expected from an indica-leaning structure. Indoor plants usually finish around 90–120 cm and produce roughly 450 g/m², while outdoor specimens in warm climates can exceed 550 grams each. Add a 63–70-day bloom and an effect that travels from cerebral uplift into full-body relaxation, and Pumpkin Spice becomes far more than a seasonal name. It is a practical American-style hybrid with a distinctive savory-fruit flavor profile and enough structural consistency to suit both newer and experienced cannabis growers.
Genetics and Lineage

The official Sensi Seeds Research pedigree is Sour Apple × Animal Cookies. Sour Apple contributes the sharper fruit character and much of the uplifting side of the experience. The strain is widely associated with Sour Diesel and Cinderella 99 ancestry, combining the fuel, citrus, and cerebral energy of Sour Diesel with the sweeter fruit and fast-finishing qualities connected to Cinderella 99. In Pumpkin Spice, that genetic influence is most apparent in the fresh apple note, the lighter mental opening, and the way sweetness cuts through the otherwise earthy aromatic base.

Animal Cookies, also known as Animal Crackers in some circles, is a cross of Girl Scout Cookies and Fire OG . Girl Scout Cookies contributes dense resin, sweet dough, earthy spice, and substantial potency, while Fire OG reinforces Kush structure, fuel, pine, and heavier body effects. That combination gives Animal Cookies an unmistakably rich personality and provides Pumpkin Spice with much of its compact plant shape, dense flower formation, and relaxing second half.

Bringing these two parents together creates a hybrid where neither side disappears. Sour Apple supplies fruit, freshness, and cerebral movement; Animal Cookies adds weight, earth, spice, and resin. The resulting 50/50 classification is therefore more than a numerical label. Its vegetative morphology looks indica influenced, its flowers grow in long sativa-like spears, and its effects move naturally from one side of the spectrum to the other over the course of the session.
Effects and Experience

The first noticeable phase develops in the head. A light cerebral tingle can appear before mood begins to rise, producing a happier and more mentally open state without immediately making the body heavy. Creative activities may feel more interesting, conversation can become easier, and ordinary entertainment tends to gain more texture. The stimulation is not usually as sharp as a pure sativa; there is an underlying softness that keeps the initial uplift from becoming excessively restless.

Relaxation arrives gradually rather than replacing the cerebral stage all at once. A warm physical calm spreads from the upper body downward, and muscular tension begins to feel less prominent while the brighter mood remains present. This overlap gives the cultivar much of its appeal. Moderate amounts may remain social and pleasantly functional, while larger servings shift the balance toward quieter activity and a stronger desire to unwind.

Sensi Seeds does not publish a standardized THC figure for Pumpkin Spice, so strength should be judged from the actual harvest whenever laboratory testing is available. Phenotype, lighting, nutrition, harvest maturity, and curing can all influence cannabinoid concentration. Consumers with limited tolerance should still approach potent cannabis gradually, particularly because the initially upbeat phase can encourage additional consumption before the slower physical effects have fully developed.
Medical Benefits

The progression from mental uplift into physical relaxation may appeal to medical cannabis consumers looking for a strain that does not begin with immediate sedation. During the earlier stage, the change in mood may make stress, low motivation, or mental fatigue feel less dominant. The creative and socially comfortable quality can also make moderate servings easier to incorporate into late-afternoon or early-evening routines.

As the body effect strengthens, muscular tension and general discomfort may become easier to ignore. Larger amounts can make rest more attractive and may increase appetite for some consumers. The strain’s balanced nature means it is not automatically suited only to daytime or nighttime use; dose has a major influence on whether the experience remains mentally engaging or settles into a much more relaxed state.

Because Sensi Seeds does not publish a fixed CBD percentage or standardized terpene analysis for the cultivar, medical use should be guided by batch-specific testing whenever possible. Sweetness, apple, earth, spice, and pine describe the sensory profile, but those flavors alone do not establish a predictable medical outcome. Personal THC sensitivity, medications, serving size, and previous response to marijuana remain more useful indicators.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aroma develops in layers rather than presenting one dominant note. During vegetative growth and early flowering, the plant carries relatively mild floral and herbal scents that are easier to manage than the aggressive odor of many Skunk or Diesel hybrids. As flowers mature, sweetness becomes more noticeable and earth begins to fill out the background. The final cured bouquet is considerably more expressive than the living plant initially suggests.

Apple is the unexpected centerpiece. It appears as a juicy, lightly sweet fruit note rather than artificial candy, sitting above warm earth and herbal character. That combination is what gives the strain its seasonal personality. The spice does not resemble cinnamon or clove in a literal sense; instead, it emerges as a dry, pine-like warmth that becomes more obvious on the palate than in the jar.

Flavor begins with sweet apple before moving into spicy pine, earth, and herbs through the middle of the inhale. The exhale can feel drier and more savory, leaving behind a mild sweetness rather than heavy sugar. Vaporization tends to preserve the fruit and herbal notes most clearly, while combustion emphasizes earth and spice. A patient cure is especially useful because the apple character becomes more distinct once the harsher green notes from freshly dried flower have faded.
Growing Information

Pumpkin Spice grows with a compact, bushy structure that makes it well suited to indoor spaces with limited headroom. Plants generally finish around 90–120 cm indoors, with tight internodal spacing and substantial leaf mass. That density makes regular defoliation useful, especially in the center of the canopy where stagnant air can develop. Adequate circulation is important because the plant naturally produces a thick wall of foliage even without aggressive training.

Flowering takes approximately 63–70 days. Indoor production averages around 450 g/m², a strong result considering the modest height. Multiple large colas rise above the plant, and the flowers take on long spear-like shapes while remaining dense and chunky. Sensi Seeds notes that the cultivar does not require extensive training, although Sea of Green can take advantage of its upright flowering structure. Soil, coco , hydroponic systems, and living soil are all suitable cultivation approaches.

Outdoor plants generally exceed 100 cm and can produce more than 550 grams each in warm, sunny conditions. Mediterranean-style climates are particularly well suited because this cannabis variety benefits from a long season and consistent light. The combination of dense foliage and thick flowers means airflow remains important outside as well, especially late in bloom. Healthy plants finish with green flowers, scattered rusty pistils, and a noticeable layer of sparkling trichomes covering the elongated buds.
FAQ
What strains make Pumpkin Spice?

Pumpkin Spice was bred by Sensi Seeds Research from Sour Apple × Animal Cookies. Animal Cookies combines Girl Scout Cookies with Fire OG, while Sour Apple is widely associated with Sour Diesel and Cinderella 99 ancestry.
Is Pumpkin Spice indica or sativa?
The cultivar is approximately 50% indica and 50% sativa. Its structure leans indica with compact, bushy growth, while the elongated flowers and uplifting opening effects reveal the sativa side.
How long does Pumpkin Spice take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 63–70 days. Plants generally remain manageable in height throughout the cycle and finish with multiple dense, spear-shaped colas.
What does Pumpkin Spice taste like?
Sweet apple is the most unusual flavor, supported by spicy pine, earth, herbs, and mild sweetness. The aroma is somewhat fruitier than the flavor, while the palate brings out more spice and pine.
How much does Pumpkin Spice yield?
Indoor production averages approximately 450 g/m². Outdoor plants grown in warm, sunny climates can exceed 550 grams each under favorable conditions.
Final Thoughts on Pumpkin Spice

Pumpkin Spice works because its two parent lines contribute genuinely different qualities. Sour Apple brings fruit, brightness, and cerebral energy, while Animal Cookies adds Cookies family resin, Fire OG depth, dense structure, and a heavier physical finish. The finished cultivar does not simply taste like either parent. Apple, earth, herbs, sweetness, and spicy pine combine into a profile that feels warm and distinctive without relying on the sugary dessert character common to many modern hybrids.

Garden performance strengthens the appeal. A 63–70-day flowering period, compact 90–120 cm indoor height, yields around 450 g/m², and outdoor harvests exceeding 550 grams per plant make the strain productive without requiring a large vertical footprint. Thick foliage benefits from defoliation and airflow, but the plant does not demand elaborate training or specialized techniques to perform well.

Its effects complete the balance suggested by the genetics. A cerebral tingle develops into a happier, more creative state before physical relaxation slowly spreads through the body. That progression gives Pumpkin Spice a broader range than its cozy name implies. It is not merely an autumn-themed novelty but a carefully constructed American hybrid with recognizable parentage, practical cultivation traits, substantial yield potential, and one of the more unusual apple-and-spice flavor combinations in the Sensi Seeds Research catalog.
